why: The full registry reports 504 pass / 0 fail on the operator's own machine and 453 pass / 51 fail from
a clean clone of the same commit. All 51 failures are ENOENT, not assertion failures.
This is not a code defect: .gitignore excludes /senior-director-state/ in full, and the suites listed
below read real business records from inside it on purpose - those records carry outbound and reply
history and are deliberately not tracked.
The hazard is that 'the shared line is green' silently depended on untracked local files, so a green
run could not be reproduced by anyone else and nobody could see why. This manifest makes the
dependency declared instead of hidden, and record-dependency-declared.test.mjs fails the moment a
suite starts reading untracked state without being listed here.
note: Adding a suite here is a deliberate act with a cost: that suite cannot be verified by anyone who does
not hold the operator's records. Prefer a tracked fixture whenever the assertion does not genuinely
need the real record. Rule 14 cuts both ways - a real record is honest, and so is saying out loud
that a green result is not independently reproducible.
RUN-AP / AP4 (2026-08-05): this check scanned only ARIA Sentinel/tests/ while the registry also runs
~20 suites from the repository-root tests/ directory, so a root-level suite could read the untracked
records and never be seen by the check whose job is to see that. Root suites are now scanned and are
declared by the path the registry uses. Seven were found already reading or naming the untracked root
and are declared here rather than left invisible.
Being listed means the suite REFERENCES the untracked root. Some (deploy-safety-denylist,
probe-deploy-safety) name it in a denylist rather than reading business records from it; that is a
weaker dependency than reading a record, and it is declared anyway, because the cost of over-declaring
is a longer list and the cost of under-declaring is a green nobody else can reproduce.
